summary: Mihai Eminescu was an Indologist. He studied at Staatsgymnasium Czernowitz, the University of Vienna (1869–1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1872–1874) under Albrecht Weber.

Philosopher Mihai Șora studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1939–1945), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1959–1969).
Indologist Mihail Alekseevič Širjaev studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov (~1920–1925). He held a post as Docent of Indology at the Leningrad Oriental Institute.

Mihail Nikolaevič Sotnikov worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Docent of Indology at Leningrad Oriental Institute, Head of Indian Linguistics at MGIMO (1954–1956), and on the faculty of Moscow State University (1956–1965).
Mikael Aktor specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen in 1998 and became Associate Professor at the University of Southern Denmark in 1999.

Mikaël Bauer works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Paul Hoornaert, and earned a PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). He is attested at McGill University in 2026.

Working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Mikel Burley studied at the University of Essex (1990–1993) under J. M. Bernstein and earned a PhD at Bristol (-2005) under John Peacock. He was Associate Professor at Leeds (attested 2007–2020).

Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar Mikhail Izrailevich Tubyansky studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1919) under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Boris Vladimirtsov. From 1920 to 1937, he held posts at the Asiatic Museum, IOM RAS, and Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Indologist Mikhail Kudryavtsev studied at Leningrad Topographical Technical School (1929–1932) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1934–1939). He worked at the Institute of Ethnography as naučnyj sotrudnik (1948) and staršij naučnyj sotrudnik (1969).

Linguist and Indologist Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson studied at Moscow State University (~1909–1913) under Filipp Fortunatov, Wiktor Porzeziński, and Nikolai Trubetzkoy. He served as Docent at Moscow State University from 1916 to 1952.
Mikhail Pokrovsky studied under Vsevolod Miller and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov around 1887–1891.

Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Mikhail Sergeevich Troitsky studied at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts RAS (1928–1931) under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1928). He later held a post at the University of Chicago.
Mikhaïl Peterson studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński (~1906–1913) and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov. He taught Pavel Grintser and Vyacheslav Ivanov.
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he was attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

Philosopher and sinologist Mikisaburo Mori studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University (-1962). He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School (1942), Osaka University (1950; professor 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1983).

Linguist and Indologist Mikołaj Kruszewski studied at the University of Warsaw (~1872–1875) and Kazan State University (~1878–1881) under Jan Baudouin de Courtenay. He held various teaching chairs at Kazan State University from 1879 to 1886.

Indologist and linguist Mikołaj Rudnicki studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski at Jagiellonian University (~1903–1911). He served as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań from 1919 to 1950.

Mildred Archer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at St Hilda's College, Oxford (~1931–1977), and served as Keeper of Prints and Drawings at the India Office from 1954 to 1980.

Milena Hübschmannová worked in Indology and linguistics, completing her studies and PhD at Charles University. She held posts at the Oriental Institute (1963–1967), the Czech Academy of Sciences (1969–1974), and became Professor of Romani at Charles University in 1991.

Miles Bronson was active in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Colgate University (~1832–1836) and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School (~1834–1836), and founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.
